items.title: John Joseph Interview, 1962-01-18
items.q: He taught me. I was playing in his band.

ctx.x: Anthony Holmes. Anthony Holmes. Yeah, that was a great man. He was a good musician then. Where was he from originally? He taught me. I was playing in his band. And he said, John you took a musician to play a bass, a violin, you know? Get a shelly. You got a little shelly. I played in the band a while. And after saxophone, you got to begin to get famous once you get your saxophone. And the kind of gets you out to. You can sit down over here.
You might as well take it easy.

items.title: John Joseph Interview, 1958-11-26
items.q: Well, I was playing bass with the same band, Professor Holmes. And he said, John, you have a man like you shouldn't be on the bass.

ctx.x: Oh, where did you get your saxophone? My saxophone?

Well, I was playing bass with the same band, Professor Holmes. And he said, John, you have a man like you shouldn't be on the bass. I got a shell, see? And I got the shell, played the shell a while, and said, why don't you get your saxophone? I'll get you saxophone pretty cheap. So, a friend of mine was there at the time, they said, I know a fella in Yardin. Just came from New York with a saxophone. I just bought it. So, I gave him, they said he wanted fifty dollars for it, and I gave him fifty dollars to train…
And you played it with the Holmes band?
